text:
mira: bringing up lichen3b v0.9 (int8) on staging — seeing a consistent quality drop vs fp16 on our summarization eval + sporadic OOMs when batch >= 8. anyone run into this pattern?
jon: hmm, quality + OOMs together usually points at quantization mismatch or aggressive prefetch/kv eviction racing. can you paste the bench command + logs?
mira: running the bench now — pasted output below:
```
redwood bench --model lichen3b --variant int8 --batch 8 --max_new_tokens 512 --prefetch=true
Throughput: 210 toks/s
p95 latency: 860ms
Memory high: 13.2GB
Result: OOM during alloc at decoder step 3
Log: slot_compactor: reclaimed 0 slots; kv_cache: eviction_count=0
```
deepa: what are the eval deltas? rouge / ppl?
mira: rouge-L down ~2.1, ppl +5.4 on the 1k-sample regbench (same prompts we use for onboarding).
sam: try immediate mitigations: set batch=4, max_new_tokens=256, and disable prefetch. also enable soft-reserve and kv-evict-threshold=0.6 locally. gives breathing room for slot compaction.
ken: we saw a similar pattern on a different 3B where the driver scheduler interacted badly with continuous batching. kv-evict-threshold=0.6 fixed OOMs for us.
ci-bot: perf-checker/canary: lichen3b-int8 canary failed. latency +12% relative to baseline, mem spike +1.8GB. full logs: https://ci.redwood/lichen3b/runs/4421
jon: deepa — int8 mapping sometimes shifts activation ranges; did you run per_channel calibration or post-training clamp?
deepa: not yet. initial pass used global scale from the quant tool. per-channel or per-layer scaling often recovers the quality. also try bias correction for attention heads (we've seen headwise bias drift).
mira: quick manual experiment results: batch=4, prefetch=false, kv-evict-threshold=0.6, max_new_tokens=256 -> no OOMs, p95 220ms, throughput -15% but rouge-L delta now within 0.3% of fp16.
sam: that's promising. sounds like a config sweet spot for staging canary. long-term we'll want a quant recalibration.
jon: proposed onboarding checklist for lichen3b (and similar 3B models):
1) quant calibration: per-channel on 2k samples
2) run short regbench (1k prompts) for quality delta
3) mem-frag probe: microbench with varying batch/max_new_tokens to find knee point
4) canary config: batch=4, max_new_tokens=256, prefetch=false, kv-evict-threshold=0.6
5) run dedicated canary in x-region for 24h soak
6) if int8 quality > threshold, roll; else fallback to fp16

deepa: add: run attention-head bias-correction patch + eval. quantizer has an option `--head-bias-correct` that helped on hawk3b.
ken: ops note — we'll add a soft-immediate fallback route in the routing policy: if canary fails QoQ metrics, route to fp16 variant automatically.
ci-bot: checklist issue created: https://issues.redwood/ML-1123 (lichen3b onboarding).
mira: i'll create the canary config and queue the overnight eval. attaching the config snippet: 
```
model: lichen3b
variant: int8
batch_size: 4
max_new_tokens: 256
prefetch: false
kv_evict_threshold: 0.6
quant: { mode: per_channel, head_bias_correct: true }
soft_fallback: fp16
```
jon: also try running the microbench with `--mem-frag-probe` which prints reclaimed slots and high-watermark per stage; helps reproduce the OOMs deterministically.
sam: if we still hit regression after per-channel recalib, try the int4-lite fallback for latency-sensitive routes — cheaper and sometimes closer in quality for these small models.
deepa: i'll run the per-channel calibration tonight and post results in the thread. if quality recovers we can re-enable auto-quant in canary.
mira: thanks — i'll update the issue and ping infra when the canary is live. :thumbsup:
